business_scope.primary_industry_name: Carbon-Fiber Milling and Brushless Motor Integration of FPV Drones

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Federal Common Law; Quebec private law governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (civil law tradition) with French civilist foundations.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CETA - Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (Canada-EU, provisionally applied)
CPTPP - Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Canada: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17 and FINTRAC regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 16. Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (ARLEP), arts. 31-33 and Schedule I, including mandatory declaration of persons with significant control (beneficiaires ultimes) effective 31 March 2023; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2265 (limited partnership formation and partner disclosure); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access with restricted indexed fields: Quebec enterprise register (REQ) requires every registered enterprise to disclose persons with significant control at the 25% threshold; detailed UBO data (name, date of birth, address, nationality) is accessible to law enforcement, Revenu Quebec, tax authorities and other competent public bodies; the public index only indicates that a declaration exists, not the underlying beneficiary identity.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Limited partnership agreement (contrat de societe en commandite) - original or notarized copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Partners executing the instrument; Quebec notary (notaire) if executed in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization - Canada is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; foreign-executed documents must be certified by the competent Canadian consular officer in the country of issuance; if executed in Quebec, a notarial act is accepted without consular authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Government-issued identity evidence of every general partner, limited partner holding >=25% entitlement, and each UBO (passport, national ID, birth certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil registry or passport authority of the partner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization at the Canadian embassy/high commission in the issuing state, followed by certified French translation (Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent attestation from any predecessor foreign corporate registry or foreign limited partnership register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registrar, ministry of justice, or equivalent official authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by a Canadian consular officer, plus apostille/certification chain of the issuing country in compliance with Canadian consular requirements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Quebec authorized representative / registered agent for service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the partner's jurisdiction, counter-validated by the Quebec registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization of the foreign notarized original, followed by acceptance and French-language protocol before a Quebec notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory before REQ registration: positive identification and verification of all partners and UBOs (25% threshold) against the UN Security Council consolidated list, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act regulations), and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) enforcement measures; for all USD payment rails, OFAC SDN screening is also mandated. Given the Low_Risk_Standard banking tier for FPV drone retail (ISIC 3240), simplified but fully documented Customer Due Diligence is permitted under PCMLTFA; a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) assessment and ongoing transaction monitoring protocol must be adopted by the LP's AML compliance officer and reviewed by the designated service provider.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - official enterprise register portal; name reservation through REQ-004-A application at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory French-language designation under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11). The partnership name must be expressed in French unless a legally recognized foreign name is registered with a French version. Legal suffix must be 'societe en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'; a person may also use the English equivalent 'limited partnership'/'L.P.' only as a recognized alternate designation. The name must be composed of Latin letters, Arabic digits, apostrophes, periods, hyphens, and standard French accents; no other symbols or scripts are accepted. Every name requires transliteration into French phonetics when of foreign origin.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canada / Quebec / Montreal (requires express authorization of the relevant federal/provincial or municipal authority)
Crown / royal / royale (requires royal assent authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension of a REQ name reservation is permitted; after expiry, a fresh REQ-004-A application with a new reservation fee must be filed. Upon rejection of a name, the applicant may: (1) file a written reconsideration request with the REQ directorate within 30 days of the notice, submitting alternate name variants and a written legal argument addressing the distinctiveness criteria under art. 32 ARLEP; (2) if reconsideration is refused, institute a judicial review application before the Court of Quebec in the district of the REQ's principal office within 60 days of the refusal, pursuant to arts. 529 and 866 of the Code of Civil Procedure; (3) simultaneously proceed with a new reservation application for a modified name to avoid operational delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this low-risk e-commerce retail segment, subject to conditions: the REQ declaration must state a physical address for the principal establishment and an executive office in Quebec; mail-forwarding virtual offices are accepted for service of process provided legal process can be physically served at the registered agent's address; however, Revenue Quebec and Revenu Quebec may challenge pass-through benefits if no minimum business substance is maintained (open mail, local bank account, import/billing records); a physical location is recommended for hobby-drone inventory storage and to support GST/QST registration. No Transport Canada aviation license applies to retail sales of FPV racing drones, but import/operation of drones remains separately regulated.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: LOW to MODERATE - approximately 12% cumulative probability over the first three years of an unannounced place-of-establishment verification by Revenu Quebec for a registrant in e-commerce retail; inspections are typically triggered by UBO filing anomalies, tax return mismatches, or PEP/sanctions alerts, not by the industry sector alone.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ), arts. 2186 and 2236 et seq. (limited partnership), read with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 7, 19, 25 and 30; no separate Companies Act applies to a limited partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar), Direction de l’immatriculation, Revenu Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d’immatriculation d’une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital under the Civil Code of Québec and no statutory escrow account requirement for a limited partnership. Limited partners must contribute the capital agreed in the partnership contract, and their liability is limited to the unpaid portion of that contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [●] SOCIÉTÉ EN COMMANDITE / LIMITED PARTNERSHIP. BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The limited partnership is constituted under arts. 2236 et seq. C.c.Q., and the capital subscription of each limited partner set out in the partnership agreement is accepted. 2. The registered office is fixed at [●], Quebec, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is authorized to file all registration declarations. 3. [●] is appointed Chief Manager and [●] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer, each with authority to act for the General Partner. 4. Such officers, acting alone, may open banking accounts, execute registry declarations, obtain licences, and otherwise carry on the carbon-fiber milling and brushless-motor FPV drone business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed limited partnership name through the Registrar’s online services. Verify that the name contains a legal designation such as 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C./L.P.' and does not falsely suggest incorporation. Obtain the name reservation certificate before filing the registration declaration.
required_dossiers: Legal form of enterprise: limited partnership
Identity proof for the general partner(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name request or a written explanation with the Registrar within 30 days, presenting alternative distinct names and any consent from holders of confusing names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties in private contract; Quebec notary if desired
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a written société en commandite contract in English or French. State capital contributions, profit/loss allocation, management authority, general partner powers, limited partner restrictions, withdrawal and dissolution terms. Notarization is not mandatory unless immovable property is contributed or a bank requires it; keep signed originals in partnership records.
required_dossiers: Resolution appointing initial manager of the general partner
Consent of registered office owner or lease
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a statement in the contract conflicts with registry records, amend the contract by a supplementary written resolution and, where applicable, file a correcting declaration; no public filing of the agreement is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory registration of the limited partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online filing portal at Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Déclaration d’immatriculation d’une société en commandite. Identify the partnership name, registered office and principal establishment in Quebec, general partner(s) and residence, limited partner(s), and stated contributions. Authenticate the signatory and submit. Maintain a copy of the registry extract as proof of formation.
required_dossiers: Government-issued identification of general partners and signatory
Proof of Québec establishment (lease, ownership or address consent)
Authorization from general partner to sign the declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried for incomplete or inaccurate data, file an amending or correcting declaration with the Registrar within 15 days; if the statutory deadline passes, apply for reinstatement or late correction under P-44.1 and pay any prescribed late or registry charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain taxation and employer identification accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the assigned NEQ to register with Revenu Québec for QST and, if employing staff, source deductions and CNESST employer account. Register separately with CRA for GST/HST if annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; consider voluntary GST/HST registration to claim input tax credits. Keep all accounts in the partnership name.
required_dossiers: Payroll and employer information, if applicable
Banking authority resolution for direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax account activation is rejected, reconcile the name, address and officer details in the Quebec enterprise registry with Revenu Québec and CRA records; resubmit corrected application within 30 days.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal income tax and GST/HST; Revenu Québec (RQ) for Quebec income tax, QST, and payroll source deductions; business registry: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ). Portals: CRA My Business Account and RQ Mon dossier d'entreprise / CléNumérique.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: register the LP with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain an 11-digit NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) via the immatriculation declaration for sociétés en commandite. Step 2: after NEQ issuance, apply for the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 by mail/fax (or Business Registration Online where the agent holds a Canadian credential); request GST/HST program account (BN + 'RT') and, if applicable, payroll program account (RP). Step 3: apply to Revenu Québec for the QST registration using Form LM-1-V (or online under Mon dossier d'entreprise with the NEQ and an authorization mandate); RQ issues a QST number linked to the NEQ in the 'TQ' series. Step 4: file the partnership information return T5013 (CRA) and CO-17 (RQ) annually, allocating income to partners. Step 5: non-resident partners must provide their foreign TINs and residence declarations to the LP; the LP must withhold and remit the 25% Part XIII tax (treaty-reduced if applicable) on non-resident partners' shares of Quebec business income unless the partner files a Part I return for the year. Step 6: maintain a designated partnership representative for CRA/RQ correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — An LP is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax purposes: no entity-level federal or Quebec income tax; each partner includes its allocable share of partnership income or loss in its own return. For GST/HST/QST, however, the partnership is itself a separate person and registrant and must charge, collect and remit GST and QST on taxable supplies and claim input tax credits (ITCs/RTDs). Canada does not provide check-the-box classification; the LP classification is statutory (ITA s. 96 and Quebec Taxation Act arts. 596 et seq.). Territorial scope: resident partners are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxable in Canada only on Canadian-source business income derived through the LP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada. Available elections for an LP include: (i) partnership fiscal-period election (ITA s. 249.1 and Quebec parallel) to adopt a non-calendar fiscal year; (ii) ETA s. 273 partnership/member election to treat the partner as supplier/recipient for GST/HST/QST purposes (ITC attribution); (iii) ITA s. 216(1) election for non-resident partners to compute Canadian tax on a net basis on specified Canadian-source income instead of gross Part XIII withholding, with a Quebec mirror under the Taxation Act; (iv) hybrid mismatch regime under ITA ss. 18.4-18.6 (BEPS Action 2) and Quebec conforming rules: these are disallowance and relief rules, not elective classifications, but an LP that is a hybrid entity must apply them to cross-border payments between partners and foreign transparent entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) at 9.975%; combined statutory VAT-equivalent rate for supplies made in and delivered to Quebec is 14.975% (QST is computed on the same GST-exclusive base since the 2013 harmonization; outside Quebec only 5% GST applies, and HST provinces apply single rates of 13-15%).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the small-supplier threshold for both GST/HST (ETA s. 148) and QST (Taxation Act): registration becomes mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies of the person and its associated persons exceed CAD 30,000 in the current calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; registration must be completed within 29 days of the quarter end. For the FPV drone retail business via PayPal/Stripe, the LP should register voluntarily before reaching the threshold in order to claim ITCs/RTDs on drones, carbon-fiber materials, brushless motors, freight, and warehousing inputs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not impose mandatory e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, or digital stamping. Requirements: (i) every GST/HST/QST invoice must state the supplier's BN and GST/HST registration number (and QST number where applicable), the invoice date, the description of goods, the consideration, and the amount of tax payable or a 0% export indication; (ii) invoices issued by a Quebec supplier must be drawn up in French under the Charter of the French Language, whether paper or electronic; (iii) e-invoices are accepted if kept in a readable format for six years and exchanged with the recipient's consent; (iv) CRA and RQ accept XML/EDI remittance, GST/HST NETFILE, and RQ e-Services; the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework (PCTF) and PEPPOL interoperability are being adopted for B2B e-invoicing but are not yet mandatory; (v) no certified fiscal-device or API-clearance requirement applies to e-commerce sales processed via Stripe or PayPal, but gateway receipts must display the registration numbers and applicable taxes when GST/QST is collected.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies when a supplier sells tangible personal property (FPV racing drones, spare parts) to a non-resident recipient and the goods are exported as part of the supply, i.e., shipped by the supplier from Canada to a destination outside Canada and exported as soon as is reasonable after the sale (ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 1; QST mirror in the Quebec Taxation Act). Services supplied to non-residents, such as remote tuning or consulting, may also be zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V s. 7 provided the service is not performed on goods located in Canada and the recipient is outside Canada. The sale must be reported in the GST/QST net tax calculation as zero-rated, preserving entitlement to ITCs/RTDs on all Canadian input costs including carbon-fiber components, brushless motors, milling costs, warehouse, and freight. Zero-rating is denied if the goods are sold to a Canadian resident, delivered in Canada, or accompanied by insufficient export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice showing seller BN/RT and QST numbers, Incoterms, destination country, and 0% export indication

CBSA e-manifest or export record (a formal CAED export declaration is required only for controlled or permit goods; hobby drones are generally CAED-exempt, but the courier or forwarder's export manifest must identify the shipment as a Canadian-origin export)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or courier consignment note showing pickup in Canada and delivery outside Canada (e.g., DHL, FedEx, UPS)
Foreign customs entry or delivery proof (e.g., US CBP entry summary, postal or courier tracking showing delivered status abroad)
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or PayPal/Stripe settlement statements evidencing receipt of the foreign consideration
Purchase order, contract, and correspondence identifying the non-resident buyer's registered address
T5013 partnership return and GST/QST working papers retained for the six-year CRA/RQ record period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline on export proceeds; the 180-day convention reflects the CRA/RQ audit-evidence window, under which payment should be received and the corresponding inward remittance document obtained within approximately six months of shipment to substantiate zero-rating. On audit, CRA and Revenu Québec may disallow zero-rating for deficient documentation and reassess the supplies as taxable at the combined 14.975% rate, claw back the export-related ITCs/RTDs previously claimed, and charge prescribed daily compound interest (2025 prescribed rate approximately 8%) plus penalties: (i) false statement or omission penalty under ETA s. 280.1 equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 5% of the net tax sought to be evaded, with an equivalent QST penalty under the Quebec Tax Administration Act; (ii) gross-negligence fines and imprisonment for tax evasion under ETA s. 327 and ITA s. 239, with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded; (iii) unlimited reassessment periods where misrepresentation is attributable to fraud or wilful default; (iv) Revenu Québec may suspend or revoke the LP's QST registration; and (v) the general partner(s) of the LP are jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/QST, interest, and penalties under ETA s. 323 and the parallel Quebec provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a regime of full current account convertibility administered by the Bank of Canada with no quantitative restrictions on repatriation of profits earned by limited partnerships. Capital account transactions remain subject to prior approval thresholds for portfolio investments exceeding CAD 5 million per counterparty; operational FX needs for trade finance and hedging fall outside these controls. Profit remittance is unrestricted once tax filings are complete and beneficial ownership is verified, subject only to standard AML screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists for surrender of export proceeds. Receipts from international sales of FPV drone components and accessories are freely convertible and repatriable without mandated conversion ratios or timelines. Export declarations under the Export and Import Permits Act are required only where controlled items are involved; retail hobby-grade drone transactions trigger no such obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for PayPal and Stripe as retail payment rails. Legal constraints center on compliance with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, PCI-DSS standards, and PIPEDA for cross-border data flows. Offshore digital EMIs are permissible provided the Canadian LP maintains proper registration as a money services business or uses licensed processors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding via Canadian bank portals and video KYC is fully permitted for Quebec limited partnerships. Directors or authorized signers must complete identity verification; physical appearance is not mandatory but may be required for enhanced due diligence on non-resident beneficial owners or complex ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership agreement, certificate of formation from Registre des entreprises du Québec, beneficial ownership register, and source-of-funds evidence
Business plan, product certifications, sales invoices, and projected revenue documentation to substantiate low-risk retail FPV drone operations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 wires to the Canadian bank account. Purpose codes include EQ for equity contributions and LOAN for partner loans. All transfers require matching beneficiary details, reference to the limited partnership name, and supporting capital contribution resolutions. Verification is mandatory under FINTRAC guidelines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements cleared through SWIFT MT103 for standard trade payments or via commercial letters of credit for larger transactions. All disbursements require pre-approved trade documentation, commercial invoices, and proof of goods receipt. No export license is required for retail hobby-grade drone components.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Enterprise Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the initial registration, as notified by reminder from the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is penalized by prescribed monetary penalties; continued non-compliance for two consecutive years may cause radiation (strike-off) of the limited partnership registration, with resulting loss of the statutory limitation of liability of limited partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and partner slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the fifth month after the end of the partnership's fiscal period (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file incurs a minimum $100 penalty; if the return is filed late, penalties include 5% of overdue amounts plus 1% per month (to 12 months), and each late T5013 slip attracts a $50 per day penalty, up to $7,500 per return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec Partnership Information Return (TP-600) and relevant relevés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the partnership to a penalty of $50 per day up to $1,500, and further penalties if the late return is filed more than 12 months after the due date; partners' delinquency may also be subject to administrative fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a Quebec société en commandite under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Act respecting the publicity of enterprises. An audit becomes mandatory only where required by the limited partnership agreement, a creditor or investor covenant, or specific structuring where the partnership is treated as a 'large partnership' under the Income Tax Act (cost amount of partnership property generally at least CAD 5 million) and an audited statement is demanded by the taxing authority or regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP as selected by the general partner: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); the T5013 return must be prepared using the same accounting framework consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a Quebec limited partnership, shareholding transfers are not applicable; partnership interests are recorded internally. The annual enterprise declaration to the Registraire des entreprises serves as the annual confirmation of beneficial ownership: the partnership must confirm and disclose any individual who directly or indirectly holds or controls 25% or more of the partnership interests. Any change in the identity or percentage of such beneficial owners during the year must also be reported by the general partner in a supplementary update declaration within 15 days of the occurrence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of limited and general partners (names, addresses, contributions and profit-sharing percentages)
Minute book of partnership decisions and resolutions of the general partner
Register of transfers and assignments of partnership interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - 600 per year for a Quebec registered office service and agent for service of process
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 8,000 if a certified audit is imposed by a lender or partner; not otherwise incurred for a small retail FPV drone LP

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate rate 15.0%; Quebec general corporate rate 11.5%; combined general headline rate for a corporate partner deriving business income through the Quebec limited partnership is 26.5% (2025). The LP itself is fiscally transparent and does not pay corporate income tax; each partner is taxed on its allocable share.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No partnership-level tax. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partner may claim the federal small business deduction on up to CAD 500,000 of active business income, yielding a combined federal/Quebec reduced rate of approximately 12.2% for 2025. Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) credits reduce effective tax: federal refundable ITC of 33% for eligible CCPC expenditures; Quebec refundable R&D credit of 14% for large enterprises and up to 30% for SMEs. Qualifying small business capital gains may further benefit from the lifetime capital gains exemption.
